```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(reindeer)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
corp <- demo_corpus()
n <- function(q) nrow(collect(query(corp, q)))
```

`query()` understands the full EMU Query Language (EQL). Results are
`segment_list`s: tibbles with one row per segment and times in
milliseconds.

## Simple queries

```{r simple}
n("Phonetic == t")            # equals
n("Phonetic != t")            # not equals
n("Phonetic =~ '[ptk]'")      # regular expression
n("Phonetic !~ '[ptk]'")      # does not match
n("Phonetic == t|k|p")        # one of several labels
```

A query names a level (`Phonetic`) and optionally an attribute
(`Word:Text`). Labels with special characters are quoted with single quotes.

## Sequences, dominance and conjunction

```{r compound}
n("[Phonetic == n -> Phonetic == t]")        # n directly followed by t
n("[Syllable == S ^ Phonetic == @]")         # strong syllables containing @
n("[Text == the & Word == F]")               # the same word has both labels
n("[Phonetic == t | Phonetic == k]")         # either
```

`->` and `^` take exactly two operands; to chain them, nest brackets:
`[[A -> B] -> C]`. `&` and `|` chain freely.

## Projection

`#` picks which side of a compound query you get back.

```{r projection}
both  <- collect(query(corp, "[Phonetic == n -> Phonetic == t]"))
first <- collect(query(corp, "[#Phonetic == n -> Phonetic == t]"))
both  |> select(labels, start, end) |> head(3)    # the span n..t
first |> select(labels, start, end) |> head(3)    # just the n
```

## Position and count functions

```{r functions}
n("[Phonetic =~ .* & Start(Syllable, Phonetic) == 1]")   # first phone of a syllable
n("[Syllable =~ .* & Num(Syllable, Phonetic) >= 3]")     # syllables with 3+ phones
```

These work across any number of hierarchy levels.

## Moving along and through the annotation

`scout()` moves along a level; negative steps go backwards. `move_to()` moves
up or down the hierarchy, the direction coming from the corpus definition.

```{r navigate}
stops <- collect(query(corp, "Phonetic == t"))
next_phone <- scout(stops, 1)
prev_phone <- scout(stops, -1)
syllables  <- move_to(stops, "Syllable")        # up
phones     <- move_to(syllables, "Phonetic")    # down: one span per syllable
c(stops = nrow(stops), next_phone = nrow(next_phone), syllables = nrow(syllables))
syllables |> select(labels, start, end) |> head(3)
```

## Lazy queries and provenance

`query()` does not touch the data until you ask for it, so a long pipeline
can be built up and optimised as a whole. Adding steps never changes the
plan you started from.

```{r lazy}
plan <- query(corp, "Phonetic == t")
class(plan)[1]
longer <- scout(plan, 1, collect = FALSE)       # still a plan, with one more step
c(plan = nrow(plan), longer = nrow(longer))
class(collect(longer))[1]
```

Every verb records what it did to the rows, so you can ask where segments
went:

```{r provenance}
res <- collect(longer)
provenance(res)
dropped(res)
```

A step that loses more than a quarter of the rows warns, so silent row loss
does not go unnoticed (change the threshold with
`options(reindeer.loss_warn = 0.25)`).

```{r loss}
tryCatch(scout(stops, 500), warning = function(w) conditionMessage(w))
```
